acceptance: Test: with an existing database and force_recreate, the PySpark adapter recreates it at the first connection and not afterwards.
The PySpark contract-test case asserts force_recreate acts.
context: Source: independent review and author report of PR #2632 (2026-10-04). The file path is a best guess; confirm with grep.
description:
## Problem (observed by a reviewer and the contract-test author reading code and running fakes)
In the PySpark adapter, `create_connection` runs the existing-database check before the Spark session is created. The check therefore always reports no database, and `--force-recreate` does nothing at the first connection.

## Change
- Create the session first (or run the check against the session once it exists), then decide reuse or recreate once per run.
- Add a PySpark case to the contract test that exercises force_recreate (the current case only records that it never acts).

## Guardrails (must preserve)
- The once-per-run decision guard from the mid-run item; reuse behaviour for existing databases.

## Process guardrails
- One PR per item against `develop`, via the AGENTS.md worktree flow.
- Verification ladder: `uv run -- python -m pytest -m fast -q`, `uv run -- ruff check .`, `uv run -- ruff format --check .` and `uv run -- ty check`; then `make pr-preflight` and `make pr-open`.
- Stage explicit paths; never `git add -A`. Re-read every anchor before editing.
